newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Lufthansa aims for 1997 profit lift.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Lufthansa aims for 1997 profit lift.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG, seeking to rebound from a 1996 slump, said on Wednesday it was on course for markedly higher 1997 profits after posting a first-quarter profit for the first time.

"The year has started well for Lufthansa. If we manage to maintain the momentum of the first quarter, we ought to succeed in generating a markedly higher profit in 1997 than in 1996," chief financial officer Klaus Schlede said in a statement.
Lufthansa said pre-tax earnings for the first quarter were 20 million marks, an almost 70 million mark recovery from the 1996 first quarter loss of 49 million marks.
Shares in Lufthansa were higher in midday bourse dealings, rising 78 pfennigs to 26.78 marks, shrugging off a loss in the blue-chip DAX index, which was down 22.64 points at 3,545.64 points.

"The first quarter has ended in profit for the first time in the airline's history. In our part of the world, it is normally a loss-maker," said Lufthansa chief executive Juergen Weber at the news conference.

Lufthansa had an operating loss of one million marks compared with a 49 million mark loss last year, but financial operations, which includes income from subsidiaries and associated companies, pushed the airline into profit.
Group turnover in the first three months climbed 8.5 percent to almost five billion marks, with 90 percent of the sales coming from passenger and freight services.
The balance of the group's revenues came from Lufthansa's aero-engineering services and its LSG catering business, raising the group's total sales to 5.28 billion marks.

The airline in 1996 reported a profit from ordinary activities of 686 million marks, down nine percent from 756 million marks in 1995 despite a nearly five percent rise in group turnover to 22.9 billion marks.

Lufthansa 1996 results were burdened by an extra nearly 680 million marks due to surging fuel costs, a sharp rise in airport fees and a one-off charge for pension provisions. Lufthansa's 1996 fuel costs rose 22 percent to 1.78 billion marks.
But Lufthansa said it has already made good the downturn in earnings in 1996 in the first three months of the year.
Lufthansa realised 200 million marks in savings in 1996 from its alliances with other airlines and would make further savings this year.
The airline noted its alliance with Scandinavian Airlines System SAS alone had led to savings of hundreds of millions of marks.
Lufthansa has built the code-share alliance with major partners United Airlines, Thai International Airways, SAS and South African Airways.
Weber also said on Wednesday the airline was interested in building a similar alliance for its cargo operations.

The higher first-quarter profit figure came as traffic revenue increased about nine percent to 4.4 billion marks despite only a 1.3 percent rise in the number of passengers and only a 1.7 percent increase in freight business volumes.
"The increase in turnover was due mainly to improved yields on both passenger and cargo operations," the airline said.

Lufthansa said its fuel costs were also sharply higher, rising 37 percent to 524 million marks in the quarter, but noted a markedly smaller increase in total operating expenditures, which rose seven percent to 5.28 billion marks.
